subject: Next steps — NovaBank private on-prem (air-gapped) qualification
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Thompson <elaine.thompson@novabank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + checklist for air-gapped on-prem deployment (NovaBank)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size the Private deployment correctly. High-level notes: 

- Goal: production on-prem inference for core fraud models behind NovaBank's air-gapped network.
- Preferred deployment: fully air-gapped (no egress); customer-managed hardware in your DC.
- Expected Q3 pilot: 3-month pilot with ~200 concurrent inference sessions and burst to 500.

Open items for us to validate (can you confirm?):
1) Hardware list (GPU types & counts, CPU, RAM, local NVMe): we need model-memory and KV-cache guidance.
2) Offline upgrade/upsert process: do you prefer shipment of encrypted media, or a staging node that we push to via temporary DMZ?
3) Maintenance windows and permitted downtime (weekend windows, blackout dates).
4) HSM/KMS integration approach for key material (on-prem HSM vendor/name).
5) Any required pre-install security scans or compliance evidence beyond SOC2 (third-party auditors, e.g., PenTest reports).

I attached the RedWood on-prem requirements spreadsheet and a short air-gap checklist to help capture answers. Monica is cc'd — she'll join the next technical workshop and coordinate an SE visit if needed.

Next steps I propose:
- You send hardware + upgrade preference this week (answers to 1–4).
- We schedule a 60-minute SE workshop (Monica + Rohan) next Tue/Wed to walk the checklist and confirm install steps.
- After the workshop we produce an installation plan and timeline for the pilot.

Can you confirm those dates/options and share the hardware spec when convenient?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-onprem-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet), airgap-install-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Date: 2026-05-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + checklist for air-gapped on-prem deployment (NovaBank)

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap. Below are the answers I can share today; I'll loop in infra for more granular metrics.

1) Hardware (current planned racks for pilot):
   - 2 x servers, each with 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe)
   - Dual 24-core Intel CPUs, 1.5TB RAM total across the box, local 4TB NVMe per server for model/cache staging

2) Offline upgrade: we prefer encrypted removable media (USB or NVMe sled) delivered to the on-site ops team. We do not want any inbound network push from vendor-managed systems.

3) Maintenance windows: quarterly maintenance windows (first weekend of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) are preferred. For pilot we can allow a one-time weekend window with pre-notice. Maximum permitted outage for inference services: 90 minutes during maintenance windows.

4) HSM/KMS: we use Thales Luna HSMs; keys are available for integration but must stay behind the HSM appliance — no key export.

5) Compliance: SOC2 is baseline. For production we will need the latest RedTeam/Pentest summary and any documented hardening guides you provide.

Also: what is Redwood's typical offline upgrade verification procedure? We need assurance on rollback and a clear troubleshooting playbook.

I'll aim to get the infra leads to share exact server firmware/BIOS versions and rack power details by EOD Friday.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Thompson
CTO, NovaBank

Team —

Looping you in. NovaBank confirmed A100 80GB x4 per server, prefers encrypted removable media for upgrades, uses Thales Luna HSM, and wants a limited maintenance outage (<=90m). They also requested our offline upgrade verification and rollback playbook.

Can you please: 
- Review the attached redwood-onprem-reqs.xlsx and update the hardware compatibility tab with any flags (quantization, model memory expectations, KV cache sizing).
- Draft a short offline upgrade playbook (1–2 pages) that covers: staging the artifact, verification steps, rollback procedure, and observability checks we require on the customer side.
- Propose dates for a 60-minute SE workshop (Wed 5/19 or Thu 5/20 PST) and whether an on-site presales visit is needed.

Elaine — Monica/Rohan will own the technical follow-up. Rohan, Monica: feel free to propose an agenda for the workshop; include an item on HSM integration patterns.

Thanks — I want us to have a prescriptive plan we can hand to procurement once NovaBank signs the pilot SOW.

Neha

Thanks Neha — quick confirmation and next steps from eng/SE side: 

- Hardware compatibility: A100 80GB x4 per server is fine for the model sizes they mentioned. We'll add guidance on host memory and NVMe sizing in the sheet (will update redwood-onprem-reqs.xlsx).
- Offline upgrade playbook: we'll produce a 2-page playbook and a 1-page rollback checklist. Key points: artifact signed by Redwood, checksum verification on-device, staged load to a passive node first, smoke tests against a local test harness, and a 30-minute monitoring window before cutover.
- HSM integration: we'll document the Luna HSM binding pattern we use (PKCS#11) and a helper script that runs in the air-gapped environment to perform key lookups (no key export).
- Workshop: propose Wed 2026-05-19 10:00–11:00 PST. If they prefer an on-site presales visit, we can propose a day visit wk of 5/24 — but for the pilot install the team thinks remote workshop + a single SE on-site day is sufficient.

Action items I will own this week: update the spreadsheet with compatibility notes, draft the upgrade playbook and rollback checklist, and share an updated agenda for the 5/19 workshop by Tue 5/16 COB.
